resources.string: Set disable-verity and disable-verification flags, then flash vbmeta.img

This disables Android Verified Boot checks for the flashed vbmeta image. A modified or incompatible image can make the device fail to boot or expose it to unverified system changes. Use only a vbmeta.img that matches your device firmware. The bootloader usually must already be unlocked; this feature does not unlock it. Keep the original firmware image so you can restore it.
Choose a standalone vbmeta.img. Dioxamine validates the AVB0 header, creates a temporary patched copy, and flashes that copy to the vbmeta partition. Your selected source file is not modified.
The file must be a valid standalone AVB vbmeta image and no larger than 64 MiB. Validation happens before any bytes are flashed.
Dioxamine will set both AVB disable flags in %1$s and flash the patched copy to the vbmeta partition. This may prevent normal boot and weakens device security.
I understand the security and boot risks and have a matching image and recovery plan.
